observed: HashedMap diverged on forEach output order and, through positional iterator removal and values().remove (first match), on which entries were removed: the provider's order is its bucket layout
correction: for unordered members forEach is compared as a sorted list, iterator removal is chosen by key, values().remove is replaced by contains
lesson: an oracle comparison may only use behaviour the contract fixes; order-dependent operations need an order-free form

observed: an LRU map's equals(other) calls other.get(key), which reorders the other map: comparing equality before order would have converged two different orders
correction: the state check compares order, toString and views first, then equality both ways, then order again
lesson: read-only checks first; a check with side effects runs last and is followed by a re-check

observed: LRUMap seed 0 step 450: the provider iterated a null key but containsKey(null) was false; AbstractHashedMap.reuseEntry stores the raw key on eviction-reuse without convertKey
correction: the LRU scripts use no null key; a dedicated test asserts the provider defect and the member's correct behaviour; DIVERGENCE.tsv row
lesson: a differential finds provider defects too; record them with a guard that fails when the provider changes

observed: the empty iterators of both sides print Object.toString (class@hash), which can never match
correction: the walk records an identity toString as <identity>

observed: the performance test measured LRUMap put 1.9x, remove-put churn 3.3x and evicting access 2.3x slower than the provider (25-75 bytes/op allocated by lane growth): every recency move re-appends a slot and the lanes compact; LinkedMap get(int) is 32x and indexOf 270x faster (rank/select)
correction: fixed by STORAGE_PATTERN_PER_MEMBER (pattern LINKS for LRUMap and HashedMap)
lesson: an arrayification is chosen per access pattern: append-only slots suit insertion order and index access, link lanes suit recency

observed: LRU_REAPPEND_COST fixed: the iteration primitives became atoms (first, last, following, preceding) with two storage patterns, SLOTS (bit scans, append-only, rank/select) and LINKS (int[] before/after lanes, free list, growth keeps slot ids); after it LRU churn went 3.26x -> 1.03x and evicting access 2.28x -> 1.05x of the provider, HashedMap churn allocates 0 bytes/op; the differential still passes for every member
correction: MEMBERS.tsv selects the pattern: HashedMap LINKS, LinkedMap SLOTS (index access), LRUMap LINKS
lesson: atomize the traversal once, then a storage pattern is a member-table choice proven by the same differential

observed: M3ArrayMapLiteralsTest (the M3Culprits rule) counted in the generated members 41 x 6 and 20 x 63 (live mask word arithmetic), 3 x 32, 0x9E3779B9 and 16, and the strings (this Map), =, {}, Iterator[, ] and Iterator[]
correction: named static finals in the template: WORD_SHIFT, WORD_MASK, GOLDEN_RATIO_32, FOLD_SHIFT, TO_STRING_CHARS_PER_ENTRY, THIS_MAP, EMPTY_MAP, KEY_VALUE_SEPARATOR, ITERATOR_OPEN, ITERATOR_CLOSE, ITERATOR_EMPTY; the gate then caught one site the patch regex missed, (slots + 63)
lesson: hoist from the gate's census, not from a regex guess: the gate reports the sites a patch misses

observed: hash and sameKey had no Javadoc; hash, sameKey and insert had no performance row; four JUnit tests covered two atoms each
correction: one table generates each atom's Javadoc contract (Requires, Ensures, Effects, Cost) and its ATOMS.tsv row; one JUnit test and one performance row per atom; the tests now check Effects too (sameKey calls KEY.equals only, find and compact leave their inputs unchanged)
lesson: read the atom set by reflection and compare it with the ledger, so an atom added without its four parts fails

observed: find on a miss is 1.3x slower than HashMap.containsKey (12.8 against 9.6 ns/op): every probe of an occupied entry reads the hashes lane before it can reject
correction: open: tag bits of the hash in the index entry would reject without the hashes lane (SwissTable H2 tags); it needs a slot bound below 2^29 or a long index
lesson: a lane read per probe is the cost of the int index; measure the tag variant before changing the entry layout

observed: user directive: M3String, M3AST and M3 keys let the collection leverage the internals; keyed by an object, the ARRAY_MAP members still call hashCode and equals and box primitive ids
correction: family ID_MAP: the key is the M3 id itself (long lane, foldId = Long.hashCode, findId compares the lane with ==); the Atoms class moved to templates/ATOMS.java.inc so both families include the same atoms (generator: //#include and a PACKAGE column)
lesson: an identity that already is a number needs no object: keep it a number from the key lane to the hash

observed: the first JIT gate demanded an inline decision for every atom and failed on find (75 bytes), compact (115) and compactIds (105): C2 reported already compiled into a big method, since their own compiled code passed InlineSmallCode once String.equals or reference-store barriers were inlined into them
correction: the gate follows HotSpot's policy: an atom of at most MaxInlineSize (35) bytes must be inlined, a larger one inlined or called as compiled code, and no atom refused for size; the outcome per atom is reported
lesson: test the JIT with the VM's own decisions: an atom that is a compiled call is compiled, a size refusal is not
